extracted.intended_audience: Long-term care hospitals (LTCH) administrators, Medicare payment policy stakeholders, hospital finance officers, and public commenters on the FY 2027 LTCH PPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating Medicare LTCH PPS MS-LTC-DRG classifications, relative weights, and FY2027 standard Federal payment rate updates, including related budget neutrality, cap policies, and quality reporting measure proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-walk assignment for no-volume MS-LTC-DRGs
rubrics_metrics.description: For MS-LTC-DRGs with no applicable LTCH cases in the FY 2025 MedPAR file ("no-volume"), assign a relative weight by cross-walking each no-volume MS-LTC-DRG to another proposed MS-LTC-DRG for which a relative weight was calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-walks are based on clinical similarity and relative costliness; the no-volume MS-LTC-DRG is assigned the same relative weight and average length of stay as the cross-walked MS-LTC-DRG. Similarity considerations include care during the perioperative period, surgical approach, surgical procedure time, postoperative care, length of stay, and other resource-use indicators. When the cross-walked MS-LTC-DRG has ≥25 applicable LTCH cases, its calculated relative weight (from Steps 1–4) is used; if it has ≤24 cases and is designated to a low-volume quintile, the low-volume quintile relative weight is assigned. Adjustments are made when necessary to maintain monotonicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions excluded from cross-walk methodology (transplant MS-LTC-DRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transplant MS-LTC-DRGs are treated as exceptions and proposed to be assigned a relative weight of 0.0000 for FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: MS-LTC-DRG 001, 002, 005, 006, 007, 008, 019, 010, 652, 650, 651. Rationale: Medicare only covers these procedures if performed at a hospital certified for the specific procedures and currently no LTCH has such certification. These MS-LTC-DRGs remain in the GROUPER for administrative purposes but are assigned weight 0.0000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions excluded from cross-walk methodology (error MS-LTC-DRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-LTC-DRGs designated as 'error' (MS-LTC-DRG 998 Principal Diagnosis Invalid as Discharge Diagnosis and MS-LTC-DRG 999 Ungroupable) are proposed to receive a relative weight of 0.0000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: applicable LTCH cases grouped to these MS-LTC-DRGs cannot be properly assigned to an MS-LTC-DRG according to the grouping logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions excluded from cross-walk methodology (psychiatric or rehabilitation MS-LTC-DRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain MS-LTC-DRGs categorized as 'psychiatric or rehabilitation' are proposed to receive a relative weight of 0.0000 for FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed MS-LTC-DRGs include 876, 880–887, 894–897, 945, 946. Rationale: the blended payment rate and temporary exceptions to the site neutral payment rate would not be applicable for any LTCH discharges occurring in FY 2027, so payment under the LTCH PPS would no longer be made in part based on the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for these discharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trimmed applicable LTCH cases from best available claims data
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify 'trimmed applicable LTCH cases' from the best available data (the FY 2025 MedPAR file) to determine relative weights and to identify which MS-LTC-DRGs have no cases (no-volume) or low volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS follows its historical methodology for trimming and selecting applicable LTCH cases; public supplemental data (Table 11 and supporting files) are posted on the CMS website to show cross-walks and case identification. The system is dynamic and future counts of no-volume DRGs may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality requirement for MS-LTC-DRG updates (§412.517(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual updates to the MS-LTC-DRG classifications and relative weights must be implemented in a budget neutral manner so that estimated aggregate LTCH PPS payments are unaffected by classification and relative weight changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To satisfy §412.517(b), CMS uniformly adjusts relative weights using established two-step budget neutrality methodology so that estimated aggregate payments would be neither greater than nor less than they would be without the changes. Historical rule references provided for rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step budget neutrality methodology — Step 1: Normalization factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a normalization factor to adjust recalibrated uncapped relative weights so the recalibration itself neither increases nor decreases the average case-mix index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three sub-steps: (1.a) group applicable LTCH cases (FY 2025 MedPAR) using proposed FY 2027 GROUPER and proposed recalibrated FY 2027 uncapped relative weights to calculate average case-mix index; (1.b) group same cases using FY 2026 GROUPER (Version 43) and FY 2026 relative weights to calculate average case-mix index; (1.c) compute ratio of FY2026 average CMI to FY2027 average CMI. Multiply each recalibrated uncapped relative weight by the normalization factor (example value: 1.27379) to get normalized relative weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step budget neutrality methodology — Step 2: Budget neutrality adjustment factor for recalibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate a budget neutrality adjustment factor to align estimated aggregate payments before and after reclassification and recalibration, and apply it to uncapped normalized relative weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three sub-steps: (2.a) simulate estimated total FY 2027 LTCH PPS standard Federal payments for applicable cases using uncapped normalized relative weights and proposed GROUPER Version 44; (2.b) simulate estimated total FY 2027 payments using FY 2026 GROUPER (Version 43) and FY 2026 relative weights; (2.c) compute ratio of the values from 2.b divided by 2.a. Multiply each uncapped normalized relative weight by this budget neutrality factor (example value: 1.0037632).

rubrics_metrics.name: 10-percent cap policy on decreases in MS-LTC-DRG relative weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Cap year-to-year decreases in relative weights at 10 percent for MS-LTC-DRGs with at least 25 applicable LTCH cases to mitigate large financial impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any MS-LTC-DRG with ≥25 cases where the FY 2027 relative weight (after normalization and the recalibration budget neutrality factor) would decline by more than 10% compared to FY 2026, set the proposed capped FY 2027 weight equal to 90% of that MS-LTC-DRG's FY 2026 relative weight (i.e., FY2026_weight × 0.90). The 10% cap does not apply to new or renumbered MS-LTC-DRGs for the fiscal year, nor to low-volume or zero-volume MS-LTC-DRGs identified earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality adjustment for application of the 10-percent cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a budget neutrality adjustment so that implementing the 10-percent cap is budget neutral across LTCH payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the adjustment by: (a) simulating estimated total FY 2027 payments using proposed capped relative weights and proposed GROUPER Version 44; (b) simulating estimated total FY 2027 payments using proposed uncapped relative weights and proposed GROUPER Version 44; (c) calculate ratio of (b) divided by (a). Multiply each capped relative weight by this cap budget neutrality factor (example value: 0.997832) to achieve budget neutrality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and transparency of proposed weights and supportive files
rubrics_metrics.description: Make available on the CMS website Table 11 and supplemental data listing proposed MS-LTC-DRGs, proposed relative weights, proposed geometric mean length of stay, five-sixths of geometric mean LOS (for SSO identification), and pre-cap relative weights and cap budget neutrality factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 11 appears in section VI of the Addendum and supplemental files are posted via the CMS Medicare Acute Inpatient PPS web page to streamline public access and support annual development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 2022-based LTCH market basket for annual update
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to use the 2022-based LTCH market basket to update the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the 2022-based market basket is primarily based on Medicare cost report data submitted by LTCHs and reflects LTCH cost structures. CMS references prior rulemakings for the market basket's historical development and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory productivity adjustment and market basket calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the annual market basket update by taking the market basket percentage increase and subtracting the statutory productivity adjustment (the 10‑year moving average of private nonfarm business total factor productivity as projected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2027 CMS used IGI forecasts: proposed market basket increase 3.2% and proposed productivity adjustment 0.8 percentage point, yielding a proposed market basket update of 2.4% (3.2 − 0.8). CMS may use more recent data before finalizing. References to BLS productivity data and IGI projection methodology are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: LTCH QRP penalty (quality reporting non-submission reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: For LTCHs that fail to submit required quality data under the LTCH Quality Reporting Program (LTCH QRP), apply a 2.0 percentage point reduction to the annual update to the LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduction is applied in a noncumulative manner (applies only to the year involved and is not used in computing subsequent years). The reduction may result in an annual update less than zero for that year. Codified at 42 CFR 412.523(c)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area wage level budget neutrality and other statutory adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the FY 2027 LTCH PPS standard Federal payment rate for the estimated effect of changes to the area wage level using an area wage level budget neutrality factor and apply other statutory adjustments required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes it will apply the area wage level budget neutrality factor pursuant to 42 CFR 412.523(d)(4) and references related Addendum sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning electronic clinical quality measure (eCQM) adoption criteria and measure definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed adoption of an Advance Care Planning eCQM that calculates the proportion of adult patients with one or more inpatient hospitalizations during the measurement period who, by the time of hospital discharge for at least one encounter, have an advance care planning document or documentation of an advance care planning discussion resulting in a documented decision in the patient's EHR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: promote timely advance care planning, encourage patient-provider communication to elicit and document patient care preferences and surrogate decision-makers, support age-friendly and goal-concordant care, and standardize ACP documentation in EHRs to support health information exchange. CMS is proposing adoption across Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting, PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospital Quality Reporting, and Medicare Promoting Interoperability Programs (and references the Patient Self-Determination Act and prior Medicare reimbursement for ACP services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core elements of Advance Care Planning to be captured
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance care planning core elements include identifying a trusted health care proxy or surrogate decision-maker, clarifying care priorities for quality of life, and discussing specific treatments and interventions including resuscitation, intubation, ventilation, and ICU admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These core elements are cited as the content that should be elicited, documented, and made accessible in the EHR; CMS emphasizes hospitalization as an opportune time to initiate or update ACP documentation so directives are accessible across care settings.
